Pepper__bell__healthy.title: Pepper Bell - Healthy
advice: Crop is healthy. Continue regular irrigation and balanced fertilization.
Avoid wetting leaves; water at the base.
Monitor weekly for early spots, pests, or yellowing.

organic: Neem oil spray (as per label) for general pest prevention if needed.
notes: No medicine required when healthy.

Pepper__bell__Bacterial_spot.title: Pepper Bell - Bacterial Spot
advice: Remove and destroy infected leaves (do not compost).
Avoid overhead watering; keep foliage dry.
Do not work in the field when plants are wet; bacteria spreads easily.
Improve airflow by proper spacing and pruning lower leaves.

chemical: Copper + Mancozeb mix (where permitted, as per label)
notes: Start sprays early when symptoms appear.
Rotate products as per label guidance; avoid repeated same spray.

Potato__healthy.title: Potato - Healthy
advice: Crop is healthy. Maintain good irrigation scheduling and nutrition.
Ensure good airflow between rows; avoid waterlogging.
Inspect leaves for early blight/late blight symptoms especially in humid weather.

notes: No medicine required when healthy.

Potato__Early_blight.title: Potato - Early Blight
advice: Remove heavily infected leaves to reduce spread.
Avoid overhead irrigation; keep foliage dry.
Apply mulch to reduce soil splash to leaves.
Follow crop rotation (avoid potato/tomato in same field for 2–3 seasons).

chemical: Azoxystrobin / Difenoconazole type fungicides (as per label, rotate groups)
notes: Spray interval depends on weather and label instructions.
Rotate fungicide groups to reduce resistance.

Potato__Late_blight.title: Potato - Late Blight (Serious)
advice: Remove infected leaves/plant parts immediately and destroy them.
Avoid overhead watering; late blight spreads fast in cool, humid weather.
Increase airflow and keep field clean.
If infection is severe, consider removing severely affected plants to protect the field.

chemical: Cymoxanil-based fungicide (as per label, rotate groups)
notes: Start treatment immediately; late blight can destroy crop quickly.
Do not repeat the same fungicide group continuously.

Tomato_healthy.title: Tomato - Healthy
advice: Plant is healthy. Continue balanced fertilizer and proper watering.
Water at the base and keep leaves dry.
Maintain spacing and remove lower leaves touching soil.

notes: No medicine required when healthy.

Tomato_Bacterial_spot.title: Tomato - Bacterial Spot
advice: Remove infected leaves and destroy them.
Avoid overhead watering and handling plants when wet.
Improve airflow by pruning and spacing.
Use disease-free seedlings and sanitize tools.

chemical: Copper + Mancozeb mix (where permitted, as per label)
notes: Spray early; results are better before disease spreads widely.
Rotation and hygiene are very important for bacterial diseases.

Tomato_Early_blight.title: Tomato - Early Blight
advice: Remove infected lower leaves first and keep field clean.
Avoid wet foliage; water at base.
Use mulch to prevent soil splash.
Rotate crops and avoid planting tomato near potato.

chemical: Azoxystrobin / Difenoconazole type fungicides (as per label, rotate groups)
notes: Repeat sprays as per label interval, especially during humid periods.

Tomato_Late_blight.title: Tomato - Late Blight (Serious)
advice: Remove infected leaves/branches immediately and destroy them.
Avoid overhead irrigation; improve airflow.
Keep plants dry and monitor daily in rainy/cool weather.
If severe, remove badly infected plants to reduce spread.

chemical: Cymoxanil-based fungicide (as per label, rotate groups)
notes: Late blight spreads quickly; treat early and rotate fungicide groups.

Tomato_Leaf_Mold.title: Tomato - Leaf Mold
advice: Reduce humidity: improve ventilation and spacing.
Avoid watering leaves; water at base.
Remove infected leaves and keep greenhouse/field clean.

chemical: Azoxystrobin type fungicide (as per label, rotate groups)
notes: Leaf mold is strongly linked with high humidity; ventilation is key.

Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.title: Tomato - Septoria Leaf Spot
advice: Remove infected leaves and destroy them (do not compost).
Avoid overhead watering; keep leaves dry.
Mulch to prevent soil splash and improve airflow.

notes: Start sprays early and repeat as per label during wet/humid weather.

Tomato__Target_Spot.title: Tomato - Target Spot
advice: Remove infected leaves, especially lower foliage.
Improve airflow and reduce humidity.
Avoid overhead irrigation; water at base.

chemical: Azoxystrobin type fungicide (as per label, rotate groups)
notes: Use preventive sprays if weather is humid and disease is known in your area.

Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.title: Tomato - Mosaic Virus
advice: Virus has no direct cure: remove infected plants to stop spread.
Disinfect hands/tools; avoid tobacco handling near plants.
Control insects that can spread infection and avoid plant injuries.

chemical: No direct chemical cure for viruses
organic: Neem oil (as per label) to help manage insect vectors (supportive)
notes: Main control is removal + hygiene + resistant varieties.

Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.title: Tomato - Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
advice: No direct cure: remove infected plants early to reduce spread.
Control whiteflies (main vector) and use yellow sticky traps.
Use insect-proof netting in nursery and keep weeds controlled.

chemical: Whitefly control insecticides (as per label and local recommendations)
organic: Neem oil spray (as per label) for whitefly management (supportive)
Yellow sticky traps for monitoring and reduction
notes: Vector control (whitefly) is the most important step.

Tomato__Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_.title: Tomato - Two-Spotted Spider Mite
advice: Check leaf underside for mites/webbing; remove heavily infested leaves.
Reduce dust, keep plants well-watered (not waterlogged).
Spray water on underside of leaves to reduce mite population (where suitable).

chemical: Spiromesifen / Bifenazate type miticides (as per label, rotate groups)
organic: Neem oil / horticultural soap (as per label)
Sulfur-based options where permitted (as per label)
notes: Mites develop resistance quickly: rotate miticide groups.
Spray underside of leaves for best effect.
